## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/toggle ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Bold } from "lucide-react"; import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle"; export function BoldToggle() { return ( ); } ``` An icon-only toggle needs `aria-label`; the glyph is not a name. ## Variants Default and outline each show an off and an initially pressed button. Outline adds a border on busy toolbar surfaces; every button still toggles independently. ```tsx import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle"; export function ToggleVariants() { return (
Default Default on Outline Outline on
); } ``` ## Sizes Small, default and large use fixed 32, 36 and 40px heights. Choose one for the surrounding toolbar rather than scaling its hit target. ```tsx import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle"; export function ToggleSizes() { return (
Small Default Large
); } ``` ## With a label Text supplies the accessible name; the icon is decorative. An icon-only toggle, as in Usage, needs its own aria-label. ```tsx import { BoldIcon } from "lucide-react"; import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle"; export function LabelledToggle() { return ( Bold ); } ``` ## Controlled The caller owns the italic command. Clear italic updates this instance externally; it leaves all other examples alone. ```tsx "use client"; import { ItalicIcon } from "lucide-react"; import { useState } from "react"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle"; export function ControlledToggle() { const [on, setOn] = useState(false); return (

{on ? "Italic enabled" : "Italic disabled"}

); } ``` ## Disabled Disabled off and on commands retain their pressed state and ignore pointer and keyboard input. ```tsx import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle"; export function DisabledToggles() { return (
Unavailable off Unavailable on
); } ``` ## Inside a form Toggle renders a type="button", so its pressed state does not submit a form field. The caller explicitly maps state to a hidden input here; Save formatting reads real FormData. The second explicitly overrides that outer scope with full; the system reduced-motion preference still wins. The default press button preserves native React `onAnimationStart`, `onDrag`, `onDragStart` and `onDragEnd` events, including capture and cancellation. Callback and object refs follow the same button; replacing a callback runs its React 19 cleanup before assigning the next ref. A caller `render` replaces the default renderer and owns spreading its supplied props. ## Motion contract Recipe: `feedback.press`. The button compresses to 0.97 while the pointer is down and springs back on release. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------- | | press | `scale 1 → 0.97` | `feedback.press` | yes | | release | `scale 0.97 → 1` | `feedback.press` | yes | | reduced | no scale; the pressed background is the only change | – | – | | none | no scale | – | – | The pressed background is a colour transition, which is state feedback and stays in every mode — otherwise a `none` user could not see the state. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | ------- | ------------------------------- | | `Tab` | Moves focus to the toggle. | | `Space` | Toggles the pressed state. | | `Enter` | Toggles the pressed state. | ## Accessibility - Base UI renders a real `
